name: GenomeOcean embedding extraction throughput, peak VRAM and binning fidelity, BF16 versus FP8 weights (Yu et al. 2026 Table 3)
description: Embedding extraction on one H100 at three model scales with BF16 and FP8 weights.

attributes.protocol: Single causal forward pass over batched tokenized fragments; final-layer states mean-pooled. Throughput in input tokens per second at a fixed batch size per scale; peak memory from torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(); embeddings clustered with DBSCAN (hyperparameters tuned on BF16) and scored by ARI against species labels.
limitations: Author-reported: two authors are at the DOE Joint Genome Institute, which develops GenomeOcean; no competing-interest statement is printed.
Microbial genomes and a metagenomic-binning fidelity check, not human diagnostic sequence; the paper says the fidelity metrics are benchmark-specific (Section 4.4).
Throughput is measured at one fixed batch size per model scale, which is not printed.
Peak VRAM is printed without spread; throughput and ARI are mean and standard deviation over five trials.
One GPU type (H100 SXM5); the paper says results for other GPUs and engines need their own evaluation.

name: GenomeOcean-4B autoregressive generation throughput, power, energy efficiency and perplexity, BF16 versus FP8 (Yu et al. 2026 Table 4)
description: Autoregressive generation in vLLM on one H100 with three precision configurations.

attributes.protocol: Token-by-token generation with vLLM; throughput in generated tokens per second; GPU power from NVML at 100 ms intervals, efficiency as throughput per mean watt; sliding-window perplexity with 10,240-token context and 2,560-token stride on 96 GTDB sequences.
limitations: Author-reported: two authors are at the DOE Joint Genome Institute, which develops GenomeOcean; no competing-interest statement is printed.

Microbial genomes (96 GTDB Bacteria sequences) and a perplexity check, not human diagnostic sequence; the paper says perplexity measures sequence-likelihood preservation, not the biological function of generated sequences (Section 4.4).

Throughput, power and efficiency are mean and standard deviation over five trials; perplexity standard deviation reflects sequence-level heterogeneity across 96 fixed sequences, not trial-to-trial variation.
Generation and embedding use different engines, so their absolute throughputs are not comparable (Section 2.4).
Peak memory for generation is not printed in Table 4.
One GPU type (H100 SXM5); the paper says results for other GPUs and engines need their own evaluation.
